ActAnswer.description: `{"action": …, "ids": […]}`: what was done, and what was skipped and why.

AddAnswer.description:
An address added (`url`): the download's id, or `pending` while a torrent's files are looked
up (it joins the list once they are known).

ApiAnswer.description: `{"api": true}` / `{"api": false}`: the API's new state.

BrowserCookie.description:
One cookie as the browser keeps it (`cookies.getAll`'s fields, under the extension's names
too: `hostOnly`, `expirationDate`).

domain.description: `.youtube.com` (sent to its subdomains too) or a host name.

expires.description: When it expires, in seconds since 1970; none: when the browser closes.

host_only.description: Sent to `domain` itself only, never its subdomains.

key.description:
What `category` takes and a download's `category` says (a built-in category's English
name, as shipped).

name.description:
Its name as the user sees it: a built-in one's English name (translated where it is
shown) unless the user renamed it.

added.description: When it was added, as the list shows it; null for downloads from before that column.

error.description: Why it failed, for a download in `Error`.

id.description: What the actions take (`ids`); never reused.

path.description: Where it is saved: the file, or a torrent's folder.

size.description: Its size in bytes; null while unknown.

speed.description: Bytes per second; 0 when it isn't running.

url.description: Its address (a video's page, a torrent's magnet link).

ErrorAnswer.description: An unknown question or action, or a question while the API is off.

code.description: For programs: `"api-off"` while the API is off.

error.description: For people; its wording may change.

ListAnswer.description: `{"query": "list"}`: every download, and the total speed.

categories.description: The categories a new download can go to (General first).

free.description: Free space where downloads go (the General category's folder), bytes; null when unknown.

queues.description: The queues, in the Scheduler's order (the first is the main queue).

speed.description: The total download speed, bytes per second.

PairAnswer.description: `{"pair": true}` (#157): a new pairing code for the remote control, while it is on.

code.description: The 8-digit code; it works once, for `minutes`.

qr.description: A QR code of the first address with the code, drawn with text blocks for a terminal.

urls.description: The page's addresses, the one a phone most likely reaches first.

ids.description: Its downloads' ids, in its order.

name.description: Its name: what `queue` takes (a built-in queue's in English, as shipped).

Request.description: One request line: the token from ipc.json and the command's fields.

action.description:
Automation API: `"pause"`, `"start"`, `"remove"` (off the list, its file kept) or
`"delete"` (with its file) the downloads `ids`; answered with what was done and skipped.
`"start_queue"` / `"stop_queue"` start or stop the queue named `queue`.

api.description: Automation API: turn it on or off.

category.description: A category for `url` (its `key` in the list's `categories`); none: by the file's type.

cookie_jar.description:
From the browser: the same cookies, each with the domain, path and flags the browser
keeps for it, for yt-dlp's cookie file. yt-dlp may ask another host than the page's (a
YouTube Music page is looked up on www.youtube.com), and a cookie of `.youtube.com` goes
there too. An older extension sends `cookies` only.

exclude_site.description:
From the browser's toolbar button: leave this site's downloads (a host name) to the
browser from now on (Options → File types → excluded sites).

exit.description:
`/exit` (beyond IDM): the running app saves and quits (the installer, before an upgrade
or an uninstall). Starts nothing when no app runs.

final_url.description:
From the browser: where its redirects from `url` ended (`url` stays the address asked
for, so an expired signed link can be renewed from it).

later.description: `/a`: add to the main queue, don't start.

links.description:
From the browser's right-click menu: the links of a page or a selection, offered in the
list window to pick from (the browser's `referer` and `cookies` go with them).

pair.description:
The remote control (#157, `misterdownloadmanager-cli pair`): show a new pairing code;
answered with it, the page's addresses and a QR code to scan ([`api::PairAnswer`]).

panel_hide_site.description: From that button's menu: never show it on this site (a host name) again.

panel_show_site.description: From that button's "Turn on" (after "Never on <site>"): show it on this site again.

post.description:
From the browser: a form's download, re-sent as a POST with this body and its
Content-Type (`post_type`).

private.description: From a private (incognito) window: the download is never written to the saved list.

proxy.description:
From the browser (#42): the proxy it uses for this address ("http://host:port",
"https://…", "socks5h://…", "socks4://…"), set by a VPN or proxy extension or its
settings; or its proxy auto-config script's text. The app downloads through the same
one (Options → Proxy / Socks → "Use proxy/socks from a browser's request").

proxy_login.description:
That proxy asked the browser for a login, which the extension that set it answers with
its own: no other program can have it.

query.description: Automation API (off by default, beyond IDM): `"list"` asks for every download as JSON.

queue.description: A queue by name: where `url` waits (with `later`), or the one `action` starts or stops.

referer.description: From the browser: request context to reuse.

show.description:
`/show <window>` (beyond IDM): the running app opens one of its windows by name, for
screenshots and scripted checks (tools/lab/docs-shots.ps1): `addurl`, `batch`, `find`,
`scheduler`, `about`, `language`, `shortcuts`, `speedlimit`, `properties`, `delete`,
`progress`, `existing-files`, `video-page`, `video-helpers`, `video-subs`,
`torrent-settings`, `add-trackers`, `menu` (the first download's right-click menu),
`options[:general|types|saveto|downloads|connection|proxy|logins|sounds|regional|panels]`.

show_download.description:
That button's "Show", once a download was added: the main window comes up with the newest
download of this address (the video's page as it was looked up, or its file) selected.

silent.description: `/n`: silent — no Download File Info dialog.

size.description: From the browser: the size and type its own download had (no need to look them up).

startup.description:
`/startup` (beyond IDM): started with the session (Options → General → Launch on
startup, or the installer's "Start when Windows starts", #226): MDM starts in the
notification area, its window hidden. Changes nothing in a running app.

token.description: The `token` from ipc.json (it changes at every start of the app).

video_direct.description:
With `video_page`, from that button over a video that plays a plain file (no stream, no
page to read): `video_page` is that file, downloaded as any file at once, with no window.

video_lookup.description:
From the browser's quality menu over a video (the button's click): look this video up
with yt-dlp, off the window, and answer at once with a token to ask about it
([`api::VideoLookupAnswer`], `pending`). The browser's request context (`referer`,
`cookies`, `cookie_jar`, `user_agent`, `private`) goes with it and stays the look-up's.

video_page.description:
From the browser's download button over a video: open the Download video window for this
page (its address; an embedded player's own).

video_pick.description:
The quality menu: download the choice made there, with the look-up's own selector and
context (`private` must be the look-up's); answered `started` or `queued`, or
`use-window` when it can't be (the Download video window then does it).

video_poll.description:
The quality menu: how is the look-up of this token going (`pending`, `ready` with the
choices, `failed`, `list`, `gone`)?

video_title.description:
The title of the page the button was clicked on: a video yt-dlp knows only by its address
is named by it.

why.description:
"no such download", "not running", "already running", "complete" or "running: pause it
first".

VideoChoice.description: One quality the browser's quality menu offers.

approx.description:
`size` is an estimate (a stream's bitrate times its length, a conversion's), shown as
about ("~532 MB"); otherwise it is the bytes of exactly the streams this downloads (#801).

audio.description:
Only the sound (an audio file, a conversion to MP3, Opus or FLAC): the menu lists these
apart from the videos. False from an app older than the field.

codec.description:
The picture's codec as people name it: `AV1`, `VP9`, `H.264`, `H.265`… (#755). None
from an app older than the field.

fps.description: Frames a second, rounded (an app older than #755 said it only above 31).

height.description:
The picture's height in pixels (the button's chip: 1080p, 4K); none for the sound, or a
file known only by its type.

kbps.description: The sound's bitrate in kbit/s, for the sound as the site has it.

label.description: What the menu shows ("720p mp4"), in MDM's language.

original.description: The sound as the site sends it (not converted): the button's list says "original".

range.description:
The picture's dynamic range when worth saying: `HDR`, `Dolby Vision`, or `SDR` beside an
HDR choice of the same height (#755).

size.description: Bytes, exact or estimated (`approx`); null when unknown.

VideoLookup.description: The video the browser's quality menu asks about ([`Command::video_lookup`]).

address.description:
What yt-dlp looks up: the video's own file or its stream's manifest when the page plays
one, else the page.

store_id.description:
The browser's cookie store the page is in (Firefox's containers): a choice is only taken
from the same one.

title.description:
The title of the page the button was clicked on: a video yt-dlp knows only by its address
is named by it (as [`Command::video_title`]).

VideoLookupAnswer.description:
The browser's quality menu (`video_lookup`, `video_poll`, `video_pick`): where a look-up is,
or what became of a choice. Answered whatever the automation API's switch (the browser's
host asks, not a program).

choices.description:
`ready`: the qualities to choose from, labelled in MDM's language; `video_pick` takes a
place in this list.

message.description: `failed` with [`lookup::ERROR`]: why, in MDM's words and language.

title.description:
`ready`: the video's title, the file's name: the page's when yt-dlp knows the video only
by its address, as the Download video window names it ([`crate::Command::video_title`]).

token.description: `pending` and `ready`: the look-up's token, to ask about it and to pick from it.

VideoPick.description: A choice made in the browser's quality menu ([`Command::video_pick`]).

choice.description: The choice's place in the look-up's `choices`.

store_id.description: The cookie store the choice was made in: the look-up's, or it isn't taken.

description: One JSON line to the port in ipc.json (on 127.0.0.1), one line back. A request is `Request`. A command (an address to add, start_queue) is answered `ok`; a question is answered with the JSON object for it (`ListAnswer`, `ActAnswer`, `ApiAnswer`) or an `ErrorAnswer`. A wrong token is answered `denied`, an app that doesn't answer within 2 seconds `timeout`. The browser's quality menu (`video_lookup`, `video_poll`, `video_pick`, sent by its native host) is answered with a `VideoLookupAnswer`. Guide: https://misterdownloadmanager.com/help/command-line.html#the-automation-api
title: Mister Download Manager automation API
